cards.subject: The Forgotten Crypt
lines: There is a finished-looking dungeon under the churchyard behind Karazhan. It was present at launch and shut for years.
The level designer who built it, John Staats: "Additional quest areas. It turned out we didn't need them so I never finished them."

cards.subject: There are no quests here
lines: The wiki is flat about it: in the original World of Warcraft, Deadwind Pass had no quests whatsoever.
Every quest this zone has ever had arrived with Burning Crusade or later.

cards.subject: And nobody to talk to
lines: The friendly characters the wiki lists here are all Violet Eye, and they arrive with the raid.
There is no flight master either — you rely on Darkshire or Stonard.
You cannot fly in, fly out, sleep, sell, repair or speak to a soul.

cards.subject: The only road
lines: The land bridge east out of Duskwood, and the only overland way toward the Dark Portal.
With no flight path in the zone, everybody who crosses it walks it.
It is a corridor with a locked building in the middle.

cards.subject: The tower has no door that works
lines: It is a world model. You can walk to it and all the way around it. There is no portal, no lockout, no inside.
The raid is two years away.
The lore reason is that after Medivh was killed the tower sealed itself off from the world.

cards.subject: A woman built it
lines: The Guardian raised Karazhan on a nexus of ley lines six hundred years before the First War, as a refuge from the Council and a conduit for the lines.
Her son Medivh inherited it, was possessed by Sargeras, and opened the Dark Portal from inside it.
All of that is in the game. None of it is in this zone.

cards.subject: The land is dead because the man died
lines: Fel energy came out of Medivh's body when he was killed and blighted everything around it.
Trees "reduced to withered husks", marshes "a desiccated waste", and the sky "a sepulchral gray with the sun covered in a burial shroud".
The weather is only ever storming or about to.

cards.subject: Walk round the back
lines: The crypt door is in the cemetery behind the tower — a small decrepit church, a graveyard, a gate.
It is right there, at eye level, and it is shut.
Nothing in the zone tells you what is behind it.

cards.subject: You could get in by dying
lines: The gate turns back living players. It does not turn back spirits.
For a while you could die next to it and walk through as a ghost.
Blocked in Burning Crusade. Whether it works on any given server is a server question.

cards.subject: The room they never showed anyone
lines: One of the unfinished chambers has humans hanging upside down in the water on ropes and chains.
Everyone assumed it was cut for ratings. Blizzard denied it — "More likely we just changed our minds."
The subzone names read like a discarded design doc: Pauper's Walk, The Slough of Despair, The Pit of Criminals.

cards.subject: The ogres are here for no reason
lines: They hold the south of the zone. The wiki, flatly: no quests, and "no real use other than to farm resources".
They are also at war with the zone's giant spiders, and nothing anywhere explains why.

cards.subject: Nothing grows here
lines: "Barren and devoid of any useful resources — herbs do not grow here, and there are no precious metals to be found."
A zone in the mid-fifties with no gathering nodes in it at all is very close to unique.

cards.subject: Anonymous for eleven years
lines: The abandoned merchant camp is there from launch and nobody in vanilla could tell you whose it was.
Ariden — a charlatan who sold Medivh counterfeit artifacts and was cursed to hunt real ones forever — was only named in 2016.
In here it is scenery with no answer attached.
